key_insight: GenEHR is a generative EHR model that learns irregular patient timelines and can be adapted to stratify pan-cancer risk, including first cancer diagnosis within five years.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help prioritize patients for earlier, risk-based cancer screening, especially for aggressive cancers such as pancreatic and ovarian cancer.
method: Trained autoregressively on longitudinal electronic health records from millions of patients.
Explicitly models irregular time gaps between clinical visits.
Uses parameter-efficient supervised adaptation for pan-cancer risk prediction.
evidence_signal: In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation substantially improved prediction of first cancer diagnosis within a five-year horizon.
watch_item: These are retrospective results, so prospective validation is still needed before any clinical decision-support use.
paper_title: Generative model of patient health states and pan-cancer risk stratification
